issues.issue: Receipt date is stated as September 21, 2017 (the marketing application supporting-document letter date), but the actual NDA received date used for review-clock purposes is October 30, 2017 (filing date); however the citation does show 'Received Date(s) September 21, 2017' so this is the submission receipt—still, the card conflates submission receipt with filing; verify intended semantics.
Flagged number '60' (DOPTELET 60 mg) is a dose and should be excluded; false-positive uncited-number flag.
Flagged number '1' is part of 'ADAPT-1' identifier reference, not an efficacy/safety number; false-positive flag.
Flagged number '7' (7 days) is supported by ADAPT-1's identical endpoint citation which is explicitly stated as identical; false-positive flag.
Flagged number '4' is part of 'DOPTELET 60 mg' / ADAPT-2 wording context and not an unsupported efficacy figure; the 69%/35%/34%/<0.0001 values are all in the cited table; false-positive flag.
Flagged number '3' refers to 'supporting document 1' / 'Phase 3'; Phase 3 is supported by cited trial-design quotes; false-positive flag.

The claim '69% responders vs 35% placebo (difference 34%)' misreads the table: 35% is the ADAPT-2 placebo responder value, but the difference-of-proportion column pairs are ambiguous; ADAPT-1 difference is 43% and ADAPT-2 difference is 34%, so the ADAPT-2 placebo 35% and difference 34% are internally consistent, but the shared single p-value row does not confirm p<0.0001 applies specifically to ADAPT-2—the card's own note admits the p-value is shared, so asserting 'p<0.0001' for ADAPT-2 overstates what the quote supports.

The result reports only the Low Baseline Platelet Count Cohort and labels it as the trial result, but does not present the overall/primary population result; potentially incomplete/misleading representation of the pivotal endpoint outcome.
Citation quotes contain the OCR misspelling 'DOPELET' while card text uses 'DOPTELET'; cosmetic source-quote discrepancy.

Summary states approval was based on 'two identically designed Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials' and describes them as regular/full approval, which is consistent; however it also asserts filing October 30, 2017 as the basis narrative mixing submission and filing dates—minor internal date conflation with receipt_date field.
